identity: Nantun/Litoudian Mazu temple at51WanheRoadSection1; not a generic Buddhist pagoda.

officialPages.evidence: Official site identity and structural description:three-bay front, multiple halls, detailed carved columns.

officialPhotos.visualInspection: Direct Cultural Heritage Department photo inspected in own Chrome tab. Center roof rises above side bays; pinkish terracotta tile slopes, dramatic upturned tips and dense blue/green/gold sculpted ridges. Three dark entrance bays, red woodwork/lanterns and gray stone base.

distinguishingMotifs: Compact three-bay frontage with a taller central roof section and lower roof sections to both sides.
Deeply curved swallowtail-style eaves and prominent dragon/figure ridge ornament silhouettes.
Warm muted terracotta roof tile fields contrast with blue/green/gold decorative ridge bands.
Red/gold doorway framing and round hanging lanterns under a dark shaded eave.
Gray carved stone columns, stone steps and low base anchor the colorful facade.
materialColors: Dark red wood and warm gold accents
Warm gray stone and charcoal door shadows
pixelPriorities: Preserve the stepped roof silhouette and three entry bays before reducing ornament.
Make dragons/roof figures small decisive pixel clusters, not all-over colored noise.
avoid: Yellow Song-style double roof borrowed from Confucius Temple
Replacing every stone column with bright red poles
Inventing ritual banners or copying temporary notices
rights: Reference links only; draw original pixel art. No photos copied into shipped assets.
